summary: A monthly report of ARPANET traffic for July 1973. It tabulates, for each Host, how many packets it sent, split between traffic that stayed within its own node and traffic sent to other nodes, with daily averages. It is a data memo and defines no protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC presents ARPANET host traffic statistics for July 1973. It counts packets sent to other nodes and packets sent within each node.

questions: how much traffic did the arpanet carry in july 1973
which host sent the most packets in july 1973
what were the arpanet traffic statistics for july 1973
what did the host throughput summary measure
subtitle: BBN's host-by-host packet counts for ARPANET traffic in July 1973.

tldr.problem: The Network community wanted regular figures on traffic output by ARPANET hosts.
tldr.mechanism: The Host Throughput Summary lists packets output by host, separates internode and intranode traffic, and gives totals and averages.
tldr.outcome: RFC 556 reports July 1973 measurements and updates RFC 538. It is a statistics memo, not a protocol.

sections.title: The July Traffic Report
sections.content: A. McKenzie of BBN-NET attaches Host traffic statistics for July 1973. The report updates RFC 538 and includes a Host Throughput Summary measured in packets output.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC is a cover note for a monthly traffic table. It reports measured packet output for the listed hosts.

sections.title: Host and Site Counts
sections.content:
The table lists each host's internode packets, intranode packets, and total. Site subtotals combine hosts and include an average daily internode count and the number of days reported.

Some hosts are marked as having no traffic, and the listed sites provide the breakdown used in the totals.
sections.plainLanguage: Rows distinguish packets that went to another node from packets within a node. Subtotals group the rows for hosts at a site.

sections.title: Overall Totals
sections.content:
The final table lines give totals and daily averages for internode and intranode packets, an average per node-day, and a packets-to-messages ratio for internode traffic.

The statistics describe network output during the month and do not set technical requirements.
sections.plainLanguage: The report ends with totals and averages for the network. These figures describe measured traffic rather than defining how traffic must be sent.
